# CKC -> SurrealDB port: common lane brief (KERNEL_BUILDER sub-agent lane)

You are a read/write implementation sub-agent working for KERNEL_BUILDER on work packet
WP-CKC-posekit-overhaul. You port ONE lane of the CKC (CastKit Codex) feature set from a
PostgreSQL/sqlx reference branch onto the current SurrealDB kernel tree. You do NOT validate,
merge, commit, push, or mark anything PASS. You implement, self-check, and report.

## Worktrees (absolute paths; never create or switch worktrees)

- TARGET (edit here only): `D:\Projects\LLM projects\Handshake\Handshake Worktrees\wtc-ckc-surreal`
  branch `feat/WP-CKC-posekit-overhaul-surreal`, forked from `feat/WP-KERNEL-012` @ `1d47363f`.
- REFERENCE (read only, never build, never edit): `D:\Projects\LLM projects\Handshake\Handshake Worktrees\wtc-ckc-posekit-overhaul`
  branch `feat/WP-CKC-posekit-overhaul`. Its storage layer is sqlx/PostgreSQL. Treat it as a
  reference implementation of behaviour, NOT as a merge source. Do not `git cherry-pick`.
  You may `git -C <target> show feat/WP-CKC-posekit-overhaul:<path>` or read the reference files.
- Do NOT touch `../handshake_main`, `../wt-gov-kernel`, `../wtc-native-editors-v1`, or any `.GOV/`
  path (the `.GOV` dir inside the target worktree is a live junction to governance; never edit it).

## Hard rules

1. Storage authority is the embedded SurrealDB store via `AtelierStore` (`src/backend/handshake_core/src/atelier/mod.rs`).
   No sqlx, no PostgreSQL, no SQLite, no `pool()`, no `information_schema`, no migrations
   directory. Every `sqlx::query(...)` in the reference becomes a SurrealQL statement executed
   through `self.store().with_data_operation(|ctx| ...)` with `#[derive(SurrealValue)]` binding
   structs, exactly as the existing modules do. Study these before writing anything:
   - `src/backend/handshake_core/src/atelier/collections.rs` (`impl AtelierStore` ~line 867: `create_collection`, `get_collection`, statement consts, row structs, `write_with_event`)
   - `src/backend/handshake_core/src/atelier/media.rs` (`materialize_media_asset`, `get_media_asset`, `read_media_asset_bytes`, binding structs, `media_asset_select!` macro)
   - `src/backend/handshake_core/src/atelier/mod.rs` (`write_with_event`, `atelier_event_sql`, `event_ref_for_text`, `uuid_from_record_link`, `AtelierError`, `event_family`)
   - `src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/stage_artifacts.rs` (`INSERT_TRANSACTION`: the ONLY sanctioned pattern for committing a domain row and its event-ledger row in one `BEGIN TRANSACTION; ... COMMIT TRANSACTION;` with a post-commit re-verify). Use it for any write that must be atomic with an event.
   - `src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal.rs` (`SurrealDataContext`: `query_first`, `create_one`, `select_one`, etc.)
2. The schema is ALREADY written and hash-pinned by KERNEL_BUILDER. The tables for this port are in
   `src/backend/handshake_core/src/storage/surreal/schema.surql` (search for "WP-CKC-posekit-overhaul on SurrealDB (MT-058)",
   and the in-place additions on `atelier_collection`, `atelier_collection_item`, `atelier_action_receipt`).
   Read the exact field names, types, DEFAULTs, ASSERTs and stored discriminator fields
   (`scoped_name_key`, `active_link_key`) and code against them. You MUST NOT edit `schema.surql`
   or `storage/surreal/schema.rs`. If the schema is missing something you need, STOP that item and
   report the exact DEFINE lines you need; do not work around it with FLEXIBLE or `any`.
   Note the deliberate mappings: `atelier_tag_note.scope_ref` stores `''` for the global note
   (Rust `Option<String>` maps `None <-> ''`); `atelier_collection` uniqueness is
   `(character scope, name)` via `scoped_name_key`; composite PG keys are array record ids
   (`record::id($this.id)[0]`), see `atelier_prompt_feedback_rule_pack`.
3. Files you may edit are listed in your lane section, and ONLY those. Shared files are owned by
   KERNEL_BUILDER and are off limits: `api/atelier.rs`, `api/mod.rs`, `atelier/mod.rs`, `Cargo.toml`,
   `Cargo.lock`, `schema.surql`, `schema.rs`, `storage/mod.rs`, `model_manual/*`, `user_manual/*`,
   anything under `src/frontend/`. Your HTTP handlers go in your lane router file
   `src/backend/handshake_core/src/api/atelier_ckc_<lane>.rs` (a skeleton exists; replace it).
   It is already merged into the app router. Import shared helpers from `super::atelier`:
   `atelier_store`, `atelier_error`, `internal_error`, `calling_actor`, `header_str`,
   `artifact_byte_read_error`, `ErrorResponse`, `LIST_CAP`, `HSK_HEADER_ACTOR_ID`.
   Public types your lane adds live in YOUR module files; export them with `pub` there and import
   them as `crate::atelier::<module>::Type`. Do not add `pub use` lines to `atelier/mod.rs`
   (report the ones you would like re-exported; KERNEL_BUILDER adds them).
   If you need a NEW event-family constant in `atelier::event_family::ALL`, define the constant in
   your own `<module>_event_family` mod (pattern: `collections_event_family`) and REPORT the names
   to be appended to `ALL`; do not edit `mod.rs`.
4. Artifact bytes: the ArtifactStore (`storage::artifacts`, UUID-addressed, manifest per file,
   atomic write, hash-verified) is the canonical blob tier for CKC. Refs are
   `artifact://.handshake/artifacts/<layer>/<uuid>/payload` (manifest: `.../artifact.json`).
   Use `write_file_artifact` / `read_artifact_manifest` / `read_file_artifact` /
   `read_file_artifact_with_manifest` / `validate_artifact_content_hash`. Never write bytes to ad hoc
   paths, never to `.GOV`, never a second blob tier, never a base64 payload column.
   Resolve the workspace root ONLY via `storage::artifacts::resolve_workspace_root()`.
   Content hashes: bare lowercase 64-hex sha256 in new code; accept `sha256:<hex>` on input via
   the existing `media.rs` normalisers (`normalized_sha256_hex` / `canonical_sha256_content_hash`
   are `pub(crate)` if you need them; if they are not yet, report it and use a local copy).
   Do not add another `fn sha256_hex`; use `sha2` inline or an existing pub helper.
5. UUIDs: `Uuid::now_v7()` for every new id (HBR-INT-008). Timestamps `chrono::Utc::now()`.
6. Tests: port the reference tests for your lane onto the embedded SurrealDB harness
   `tests/atelier_surreal_support/mod.rs` (`AtelierSurrealHarness::create()`, `harness.atelier`,
   `harness.database`, `harness.storage`, `write_native_media_artifact_in_workspace`). For HTTP
   route tests copy the `app_state` + `serve` shape from `tests/atelier_media_bytes_api_tests.rs`
   (NoopRecorder/NoopLlmClient + `axum::serve` on `127.0.0.1:0`). Tests that need
   `HANDSHAKE_WORKSPACE_ROOT` must set it ONCE per test binary via a `OnceLock` (see that file).
   Reference tests that use `atelier_pg_support` / `database_url()` / SKIP-when-PG-unavailable are
   PG-era: rewrite them so they always run against the embedded store and never skip.
   Write your tests ONLY in the NEW test files named in your lane section (auto-discovered by
   cargo; KERNEL_BUILDER adds the `[[test]] required-features` entries). Do not edit other test files.
7. Builds are expensive on this host. Use ONLY your own scoped target dir and these exact shapes,
   run from the TARGET worktree root, in a hidden window if it may run long:
   - `set CARGO_TARGET_DIR=D:\Projects\LLM projects\Handshake\Handshake Worktrees\Handshake_Artifacts\handshake-cargo-target\wp-ckc-surreal-<lane>`
     (a warm copy of the dependency cache is already there; do not delete or `cargo clean` it, and
     NEVER touch any other directory under `Handshake_Artifacts`).
   - iterate with `cargo check --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml --lib --features surreal-test-support,test-utils`
   - prove with `cargo test --manifest-path src/backend/handshake_core/Cargo.toml --features surreal-test-support,test-utils --test <your_test_file_stem>`
   - never run the whole workspace test suite, never `cargo build` a binary, never `--all-features`.
   - Long cargo runs die if the agent shell is stopped: launch via a `.cmd` wrapper with
     `powershell -NoProfile -Command "Start-Process -FilePath <wrapper> -WindowStyle Hidden"` writing to a
     log under `D:\Projects\LLM projects\Handshake\Handshake Worktrees\Handshake_Artifacts\handshake-tool\wp-ckc-surreal-<lane>\`,
     then poll the log for a sentinel line. Model: `handshake-tool\wp-ckc-surreal\run-cargo.cmd`.
   - Do not run `cargo fmt` over the crate (touches shared files). You may `rustfmt` your own files.
8. Git: read-only. No commit, no stash, no checkout, no reset, no branch ops. KERNEL_BUILDER commits.
9. No new `.md` files anywhere. No edits under `.GOV`. No writes outside the TARGET worktree and
   your scoped artifact/tool dirs.
10. Behaviour fidelity: keep the reference route paths, request/response JSON shapes, error codes,
    event family names, and validation rules unless SurrealDB forces a change; when it does,
    write the change and the reason in your final report. Where the reference used PG-only
    features (pg_trgm similarity, pgvector `<=>`, `FOR UPDATE`, partial indexes, `COALESCE` in
    unique indexes), use SurrealQL equivalents (`string::similarity::fuzzy` /
    `string::distance::levenshtein`, `vector::similarity::cosine`, `BEGIN/COMMIT TRANSACTION`,
    the stored discriminator fields) and say so in the report.
11. Spec-realism: no `todo!()`, no `unimplemented!()`, no placeholder returns, no "not yet wired"
    branches, no mocks in product code. If a piece cannot be ported, leave it OUT and report it as
    BLOCKED with the exact reason.
12. Report back (final message), in this shape:
    - FILES_TOUCHED (paths)
    - ROUTES_PORTED (path -> handler) and ROUTES_DROPPED (with reason)
    - STORE_METHODS_ADDED
    - REEXPORTS_WANTED (items to `pub use` in atelier/mod.rs) and EVENT_FAMILY_CONSTANTS_FOR_ALL
    - PG_TO_SURREAL_DEVIATIONS
    - PROOF: exact cargo commands run + pass/fail counts + log path
    - BLOCKED / NOT_PORTED with reasons
    - RISKS
    Keep it factual; no claims without a command result behind them.

localhost/127.*/0.0.0.0/::1 and `llm|openai|anthropic|ollama|model-server` schemes — port the
predicate list from reference migration `0340_atelier_sheet_artifact_links.sql` faithfully.
